This is a great show. It also really 90s, and it takes a while to get going. If you want a series to sink into and then be taken on a crazy ride then treasure this chance. You will only experience Babylon 5 for the first-time once!

Watch it with friends, and get them to stick through season one with you. Babylon 5 starts off feeling comparable to other cheesy 90s tv shows because the story doesn't really get going until season two. I enjoy season one, it's not bad, but some of my friends kept wanting to stop watching the show until eventually falling in love with it later on. You have to stick with it.

Babylon 5 starts with a pilot movie, The Gathering. It sets some stuff up but it is optional, and not that great a story. After that, start watching the series. Do not watch In The Beginning, the prequel movie to the show, before you finish season four.

Fans of Babylon 5, why should new viewers start and stick with Babylon 5? No spoilers please!

Babylon 5 is available streaming on Amazon.

Like a lot of other people around here I would like to see more transparently in the modding.

I suggest you give each sub their own public ban list, which can't be removed by the person running the board. The ban should have the users name, the reason for the ban, name of the mod who did the ban and a link to the thread so people can see why the user got banned. The only tricky part is if the post contents should be left uncensored or removed (sometimes it is necessary to removal some information). Suggestion I have is to force the mod to leave a reason for the edit. Maybe even an API to pull ban from multiple subs would be useful as well but that would be down the track.
Moderation suggestion for subs - forced transparent banlists
Would be a tad difficult if the name of the poster was offensive.
This was acknowledged in the post and suggested that a reason for the edit be made and mandatory.
I don't really see why it'd be a problem.
Agreed. We aren't SJW's here, I think our feelings can stand an offensive name in a ban list.

Probably best if instead of an active link, they post a screenshot of the comment/link that got the person banned.

That way, even if the link is something illegal, those visiting said link would have to type it in by hand.

I don't like the idea of banning anyone outright, but perhaps mods could flag a user as an troll/instigator and then individual users visiting that sub could toggle whether to include/exclude people who are flagged?

That would allow each user to treat each sub they visit as either a bouncy house or a wild west saloon depending on their personal preference.
Another idea: How about limiting the number of subs a user can create/moderate to 1, and requiring a number of comment participation points for each additional sub (to a maximum of 5 or 10 subs).

That kinda sucks :(

People would make alts to get around it too.

yea, but doing it that way takes a bit more effort, compared to just being able to do it all without limits from the same account. Especially because each brand new account has no participation points, thus limited functionality (up/downvote).

I'm just thinking of ways to use the 'barrier / filter' of the participation points to try to reduce the issue of people controlling too many subs

If the stakes are higher, the countermeasures seem relatively less expensive. New accounts for more subs, if they're significant, is no cost at all. It stops casual mods from making as many ideas/jokesubs as they want, but does nothing to stop powermods from modding many subs of actual significance.

There is no perfect solution, of course.

But a mechanism that discourages the bad behaviour is better than no mechanism at all, no?

Only if it doesn't lend false credibility to those who circumvent those measures.

Say, someone who is secretly breaking that policy with alts, going around badmouthing someone with 3 or 4 mod positions because they only mod 1, if this kind of thing becomes a cultural demand/cred-points rather than just a site wide rule, it will be exploited by manipulative types just the same as legit powermodding (i.e. lots of significant mod slots on frontpage reddit) no rule on mod position limits.

Forced transparent mod actions would be nice as well, as an option maybe, maybe also the reason for deletion could be an optional thing for the mod to tag to the removal/etc, so the user(s) could see the logic in modding.

The Christmas special flirted with the idea of Clara's travels with The Doctor ending and a new companion taking place, but in the end she and The Doctor flew off for more adventures.

When the time finally comes for Clara to say good-bye, what kind of person do you think will replace her. I always thought Clara's upbeat demeanor was good after a long time with the Pond's sarcasm, even if she was a bit one dimensional at first.
What kind of companion do you see replacing Clara?
A man, older preferably. Someone who could compete with Capaldi in grumpiness.
Yeah, I feel like someone that the doctor can actually see as a friend and can actually somewhat sympathize with, instead of a girl in her 20's, would make for a much more interesting companion
Alternatively, a companion who is young but jaded and cynical could force the Doctor to be less grumpy. Or maybe just less grumpy whenever the companion is around.
I would quite like to see The Doctor travel alone, although I doubt it's going to happen

I'd like to see another really smart person, and not one from Earth. I think Nyssa is still my favorite.

I hope it'd be someone from non-contemporary Earth.

I feel like having a Roman or a Viking or a native American marvelling at the 20th century's amazingness, or else having a 30th century girl marvelling at the 20th century's barbarous backwardness, would make many of the current-day-London episodes much more engaging.
